foods.why: The pearls are cooked tapioca and the milk is fine. The tea base counts toward your 200mg caffeine day, and the sugar puts it firmly in sometimes-drink territory. As a treat, go for it.
foods.makeItGreen: Pick a caffeine-free fruit or taro base and it stops touching the caffeine tally. The sugar still makes it a sometimes drink.

foods.name: Bottled iced tea
foods.why: Bottled iced tea is pasteurised and shelf-safe, so the only questions are the gentle tea caffeine, which counts toward the 200mg day, and the sugar, which makes it a sometimes drink.
foods.makeItGreen: Inside the day's 200mg caffeine budget it is fine. It is one of the lightest caffeine hitters going.
foods.swap: Cold sparkling water with a big squeeze of lemon does the refreshing part for free.

foods.name: Iced chocolate
foods.why: Cold milk, chocolate and maybe a scoop from the tub. Like its hot cousin it counts a smidge toward the 200mg caffeine day, but it is one of the lightest hitters on the menu.
foods.makeItGreen: Well inside the caffeine budget. If it comes with ice cream, tub-scooped is the safe kind, not soft serve.

foods.name: Bottled iced coffee
foods.why: The servo fridge classic is made on pasteurised milk, so safety-wise it is sorted. The coffee counts toward the 200mg day though, and the big bottles can hold a couple of shots' worth.
foods.makeItGreen: Count it in the day's caffeine tally like any coffee and you are fine. The small bottle is an easier fit than the 750ml.
foods.swap: A chocolate or strawberry flavoured milk skips the caffeine almost entirely.

foods.name: Rooibos tea
foods.why: Rooibos has no caffeine, so the only reason it shares herbal tea's gentle couple-of-cups habit is that it is still a herbal brew. About as relaxed as yellow gets.
foods.makeItGreen: As an everyday cuppa in normal amounts, this is about as relaxed as herbal tea gets.

foods.name: Raspberry leaf tea
foods.why: This is a medicinal blend taken to prep for labour, not an everyday cuppa, and the guidance says to skip medicinal blends. Timing and dose are genuinely your midwife's territory.
foods.makeItGreen: If your care team gives it the nod in late pregnancy, that is their call to make. Pop it on the list for your next appointment.
foods.swap: An everyday ginger or peppermint tea keeps the daily ritual going.

foods.name: Liquorice tea
foods.why: Liquorice root brews sit in medicinal-blend territory, and big regular doses of its active ingredient are exactly why the skip-medicinal-blends rule exists. Not the daily brew for now.
foods.makeItGreen: If it is a favourite, it is one for the midwife chat before it goes back in the rotation.
foods.swap: Rooibos or peppermint for a caffeine-free cuppa with none of the questions.

foods.name: Slushies
foods.why: A slushie comes out of a churning dispenser machine, and the machine is the whole worry: soft serve is benched for exactly that reason. Sugar ice or not, the same question applies, so stricter wins.
foods.swap: An icy pole from a sealed wrapper, or a home-blitzed frozen fruit slushie.

split.note: The sheets never name slushies, so this is a judgement call. Here is both sides, in the open.

positions.label: The source sheets
positions.says: Soft serve and thickshakes are red because the dispensing machine can harbour listeria. A slushie machine is a churning dispenser too, though it holds sugar ice rather than dairy. No sheet rules on it either way.

positions.label: Our call
positions.says: Red. The machine rule is about the machine, not the milk, and there is no way to check the barrel. A sealed icy pole gets you the same hit without the question mark.

foods.name: Icy poles
foods.why: Straight from the wrapper and frozen solid, an icy pole has none of the machine worries. Sugar-wise it is a sometimes treat, but safety-wise, crunch away. Brilliant on nausea days too.

foods.name: Fresh young coconut
foods.why: A whole fresh fruit with a straw in it. Give the shell a rinse before it is opened, same as any washed whole fruit, and enjoy. The soft flesh inside is lovely too.

foods.name: Bottled coconut water
foods.why: Depends on the label:

variants.label: Carton or bottle marked pasteurised
variants.why: Pasteurised coconut water follows the same happy rule as any bottled juice. Hydrating, gentle, and a nice change from plain water.

variants.label: Raw or cold-pressed from the fridge
variants.why: Raw and cold-pressed coconut water skips pasteurisation, and unpasteurised juice is on the bench, same rule as the juice-bar smoothie.
variants.makeItGreen: Swap to a carton or bottle with pasteurised on the label; most of the big brands are.
variants.swap: Chilled pasteurised coconut water, or icy soda water with a squeeze of lime.

foods.name: Sports and electrolyte drinks
foods.why: Nothing unsafe in a sports drink, it is just a lot of sugar doing a job you mostly do not have. Sometimes-drink territory, handy on a truly sweaty day or when fluids are hard to keep down.
foods.makeItGreen: As an occasional thing it is completely fine. Water covers everyday hydration best.
foods.swap: Plain or sparkling water for the everyday; save these for the big sweaty days.

foods.name: Mocktails
foods.why: Depends what is in the shaker. The alcohol-free part is the easy bit; it is where the juice comes from that decides the colour.

variants.label: Built on bottled juice, soda or syrups
variants.why: Pasteurised bottled juice, soda water and syrups are all fine, so a mocktail built from them is a green light. Cheers to that.

variants.label: Made with fresh-squeezed juice at the bar
variants.why: Fresh-squeezed juice at a bar runs into the juice-bar rule: pre-cut fruit and hard-to-clean equipment.
variants.makeItGreen: Ask for the bottled-juice build, or a soda, lime and mint made to order in front of you.

foods.name: Lemon lime and bitters
foods.why: The classic LLB is built on alcoholic bitters, a few dashes of something 44 percent strong. It is a small amount, but with no known safe amount of alcohol, the strict call is to sit it out.
foods.makeItGreen: Order lemon lime and soda, hold the bitters. Same tall glass, same tang, zero questions.

foods.name: Turmeric latte
foods.why: Warm pasteurised milk with a kitchen-cupboard amount of turmeric and spice, and not a milligram of caffeine. Turmeric supplements are a care-team question, but the latte is lovely.

foods.name: Milkshake from a shop
foods.why: Depends what it is spun from. Tub ice cream and a blender is one story, the frozen-drink machine is another. The tub-versus-machine rule decides.
foods.swap: The home version from tub ice cream, milk and your own blender is a straight green.

variants.label: Hand-spun from tub ice cream
variants.why: Tub ice cream is the safe kind, but shop scoops and benches are shared, so it sits in the same careful-yellow zone as scooped gelato. A busy, clean shop is your friend.

variants.label: Thickshake or anything from the machine
variants.why: Soft-serve style machines are hard to clean properly and can harbour listeria, and thickshakes come from exactly that kind of machine.
variants.makeItGreen: Make it at home: tub ice cream, cold milk, your blender. Green light and arguably better.

foods.name: Bone broth
foods.why: Long simmering and a steaming-hot mug tick every box. Keep fresh pouches in the fridge, reheat until properly steaming, and treat leftovers like any cooked food: fridge fast, use quickly.

foods.name: Bread, cereal and oats
foods.why: Carbs are cheering for you. Toast, porridge, a bowl of muesli: all a straight yes, and the slow-burn ones keep those out-of-nowhere energy dips at bay.

foods.name: Canned and bottled foods
foods.why: Sealed tins and bottles are shelf-stable and safe. Once one is open it counts as fresh food, so it goes in the fridge and follows whatever the label says.

foods.name: Chocolate
foods.why: Yes, and zero guilt about it. Dark chocolate brings a little caffeine, roughly 20 to 30mg a row, so it only nibbles at the 200mg daily budget.

foods.name: Dips with feta or ricotta
foods.why: The dip is not the issue, the soft cheese stirred through it is: cold uncooked feta and ricotta can carry listeria.
foods.makeItGreen: Baked in the oven and served hot and bubbling, a feta dip is back on.
foods.swap: White bean dip, or a beetroot or pumpkin dip with no soft cheese in it.

foods.name: Honey
foods.why: Drizzle away. The no-honey rule belongs to babies under one, not to you. Lovely over yoghurt, on hot toast, or stirred through a mug of tea.

split.note: Zero drama here, honestly. We flag it only because the sheets never mention it, so here is the reasoning in the open.

positions.label: The source sheets
positions.says: None of our pregnancy sheets lists honey at all. The famous honey warning is for babies under one, not for you.

positions.label: Our call
positions.says: Green. Nothing in any source flags it for pregnancy, and calling it anything else would be inventing a worry.

foods.name: Hummus
foods.why: This one catches everybody out: the tahini in it is raw sesame, which can carry salmonella and listeria. Home-made counts too, because that tahini is still raw.
foods.makeItGreen: Blend chickpeas with olive oil, lemon and garlic and leave the tahini out, and it is back on the menu.
foods.swap: A home-made white bean dip, or a beetroot dip with no feta in it. Same scoop, same crackers, same you.

foods.name: Jam, tomato sauce and jar condiments
foods.why: In a pickle? Good news, pickles are fine. Jam, dead horse, mustard and the rest are pasteurised and shelf-stable: cap them, fridge them once open, mind the label.

foods.name: Lollies
foods.why: Sugar is a sometimes-food, not a safety problem. Snakes, jelly beans and party mix are all clear, so let the craving have its moment.

foods.name: Nuts and seeds
foods.why: Almonds, cashews, pepitas, a fistful of trail mix: all green, and quietly loaded with iron and good fats. Ideal for the 3pm hunger that arrives with no warning.

foods.name: Peanuts and peanut butter
foods.why: Myth busted: eating peanuts while you are pregnant does not give your baby an allergy. The one reason to skip them is if you are allergic yourself.

foods.name: Pineapple and the labour myth
foods.why: Eat the pineapple. It will not start labour, whatever the internet told you at 2am. Wash it, cut it at home, enjoy every juicy bit.

foods.name: Popcorn
foods.why: A big bowl of popcorn is a green light: light, salty and endlessly refillable. Movie night is fully approved, butter optional but encouraged.

foods.name: Raw cookie dough
foods.why: Raw egg in the bowl, sorry legend. The dough is the one part of baking that has to wait, and the tray that comes out of the oven is entirely yours.
foods.makeItGreen: Bake it. Once they are cooked through, the whole tray is fair game.
foods.swap: A warm bikkie straight off the tray, or a scoop of tub ice cream while you wait.

foods.name: Rice and pasta, served fresh and hot
foods.why: Fresh, hot and steaming is the way. Leftovers go into the fridge quickly, get eaten within a day, and are reheated once only, right through to piping hot.

foods.name: Sesame oil and toasted sesame
foods.why: Heat sorts sesame out, so oil in the wok and toasted seeds baked onto bread are both green. It is raw sesame paste, the tahini kind, that gets benched.

foods.name: Spicy food
foods.why: Bring the chilli. Spicy food is safe the whole way through: the only thing it tends to upset is heartburn, so go gentler late at night if reflux has found you.

foods.name: Tahini and halva
foods.why: Both are built on raw sesame, which can carry salmonella and listeria. It is the same reason hummus is sitting on the bench for a few months.
foods.makeItGreen: Heat-treated sesame is fine, so sesame oil and toasted seeds baked onto bread are still yours.
foods.swap: Peanut butter through the smoothie, and lemon, olive oil and yoghurt where the tahini dressing used to go.

foods.name: Tofu and soy products
foods.why: Miso happy for you two: every soy product on the shelf is safe. Tofu, soy milk, soy yoghurt, tempeh and edamame are all a yes, and all a tidy protein hit.

foods.name: Vegemite
foods.why: Enthusiastically yes. It is a folate and B vitamin hit in a jar, and spread thin on hot buttered toast it is basically a national service.

split.note: No real controversy here, but the sheets never name it, so here is the call in the open.

positions.label: The source sheets
positions.says: None of our pregnancy sheets lists Vegemite as a risk anywhere.

positions.label: Our call
positions.says: Green, enthusiastically. It brings folate and B vitamins, which pregnancy actively wants, so benching it would be inventing a worry.

foods.name: Maple syrup
foods.why: Bottled and shelf-stable, so it follows the same happy rule as the rest of the pantry: pour away, and fridge it after opening if the label asks. The pancake stack is fully operational.

foods.name: Golden syrup
foods.why: Cocky's joy is your joy too. Shelf-stable syrups are fine, so drizzle it over porridge or bake it into anzacs to your heart's content.

foods.name: Chocolate hazelnut spread
foods.why: Spread away. The jar is pasteurised and shelf-stable, and the cocoa carries only a whisper of caffeine, nowhere near enough to trouble the 200mg daily budget.

foods.name: Liquorice
foods.why: A few pieces now and then are just lollies, enjoy them. It is the daily whole-bag habit that raises a question, because liquorice root in big amounts is the same concern behind liquorice tea.
foods.makeItGreen: Keep it a sometimes-treat rather than an every-day one and you are fine.
foods.swap: The rest of the lolly aisle is wide open: snakes, jelly beans, party mix.

foods.name: Rum balls
foods.why: The classic recipe stirs rum straight through and never cooks it, and alcohol has no known safe amount in pregnancy. The biscuit and cocoa were never the problem.
foods.makeItGreen: Make a batch with orange juice instead of the rum. Same fudgy middles, none of the worry.
foods.swap: A lamington or a chocolate crackle from the same party table.

foods.name: Trifle
foods.why: Depends on the build. The jelly, sponge, carton custard and whipped cream are all fine, so the whole question is whether sherry got poured over the sponge.
foods.makeItGreen: Build it without the sherry: the jelly and custard do all the heavy lifting anyway.

variants.label: Alcohol-free trifle
variants.why: Jelly, sponge, shop-bought custard and pasteurised cream, assembled fresh. Every layer is a yes, so dig in.

variants.label: Classic sherry-soaked trifle
variants.why: The sherry goes in straight from the bottle and never gets cooked, and alcohol has no known safe amount.
variants.makeItGreen: Ask for your serve from a bowl built before the sherry went on, or make an alcohol-free one at home.

foods.name: Baked cheesecake
foods.why: Baked means cooked, so the egg and the cream cheese have both been through the oven. Even a baked ricotta cheesecake is fine, because heat is exactly what benches the soft-cheese worry.

foods.name: No-bake cheesecake
foods.why: Depends on the recipe. Most shop and cafe versions are cream cheese, cream and gelatine, all pasteurised. The odd recipe folds raw egg through the filling, and that is the one to skip.
foods.makeItGreen: Check the recipe or ask the counter: no raw egg means it is green.

variants.label: Set with cream and gelatine (most of them)
variants.why: Pasteurised cream cheese and cream, set in the fridge. No egg, no worries. Eat it fresh.

variants.label: Recipes with raw egg folded through
variants.why: Raw egg never meets any heat in a fridge-set cake, so the raw-egg rule applies.
variants.makeItGreen: Pick an egg-free recipe, or go the baked version and let the oven do the cooking.

foods.name: Panna cotta
foods.why: Cream and sugar cooked on the stove, then set with gelatine. There is no raw egg anywhere in it, so this wobbly little number is a quiet yes.

foods.name: Vanilla slice
foods.why: The custard is cooked; the honest question is how long the slice has been sitting in the cabinet. Fresh custard is an eat-it-fresh food, so a tray from this morning and a tray from yesterday are different desserts.
foods.makeItGreen: A busy bakery, a fresh tray, eaten then and there: that is the green version.
foods.swap: A lamington travels better if the cabinet looks sleepy.

foods.name: Custard and cream doughnuts
foods.why: The filling is cooked custard or pasteurised cream, both fine when fresh. Like all fresh custard it is an eat-it-fresh food, so the cabinet sitting time is the honest question.
foods.makeItGreen: A busy shop and a fresh batch, eaten today. Ask when they were filled if in doubt.
foods.swap: A hot cinnamon doughnut has no filling to wonder about at all.

foods.name: Lamingtons
foods.why: Baked sponge, cocoa icing and coconut: all cooked or shelf-stable, all fine. A cream middle is pasteurised cream, also fine. A national treasure, fully available to you.

foods.name: Anzac biscuits
foods.why: Oats, coconut, flour, butter and golden syrup, baked until golden. There is not even an egg in a proper anzac, so the tin on the bench is entirely yours.

foods.name: Fruit cake
foods.why: Depends on the booze. The cake itself is baked and fine; the question is whether it was soaked or fed with brandy after baking, because that spirit never gets cooked off.
foods.makeItGreen: Ask whether it was fed with brandy after baking. If not, slice away.

variants.label: Plain or shop-bought, no boozy soak
variants.why: A baked cake full of dried fruit. Nothing to see here except a very dense slice of joy.

variants.label: Brandy-soaked or brandy-fed
variants.why: Feeding a cake means pouring raw spirit over it after baking, and alcohol has no known safe amount.
variants.makeItGreen: An unfed, alcohol-free cake now; save the boozy family recipe for next Christmas.

foods.name: Gingerbread
foods.why: Baked all the way through, so the egg is cooked and the biscuit is yours. Bonus: ginger has a well-earned reputation for being kind to queasy tummies.

foods.name: Pancakes, waffles and crepes
foods.why: The batter holds raw egg for about ninety seconds before the hot pan cooks it right through. Cooked pancakes, waffles and crepes are all green; just leave the batter spoon unlicked.

foods.name: Oyster sauce and fish sauce
foods.why: Shelf-stable bottled sauces follow the canned-and-bottled rule: fine while sealed, fridge and label rules once open. Splash them into the wok without a second thought.

foods.name: Wasabi and pickled ginger
foods.why: Both are jarred, shelf-stable condiments, so they are fine. When sushi is the question, it is the filling that decides the verdict, never the wasabi on the side.

foods.name: Seaweed and nori sheets
foods.why: Depends on the seaweed:

variants.label: Nori sheets and roasted snacks
variants.why: Dried nori and roasted seaweed snacks are shelf-stable and green, with a tidy little iodine bonus. A sushi roll's verdict comes from the filling, not the wrapper.

variants.label: Brown seaweed: wakame, kombu, kelp
variants.why: Brown seaweeds pack serious iodine, and too much is its own problem. Keep wakame salads and kombu broths occasional rather than daily.
variants.makeItGreen: An occasional serve is fine; it is the every-day habit to skip. Nori has no such cap.

foods.name: Protein balls and bliss balls
foods.why: Depends where they came from. Off the shelf in a sealed packet is easy. The cafe cabinet ones are pre-made refrigerated food, so freshness is the honest question.
foods.makeItGreen: Grab the packaged kind, or roll a batch at home on a Sunday.

variants.label: Packaged, off the shelf
variants.why: Sealed and shelf-stable like any other packaged snack. Green, and handy in the handbag for the 3pm slump.

variants.label: From the cafe fridge cabinet
variants.why: Pre-made refrigerated food is a freshness question. Mostly dates and nuts, so it is low drama, but nobody can tell you when they were rolled.

foods.name: Instant noodles
foods.why: Cooked in properly boiling water and eaten hot, they are safe as houses. They are just very salty houses, so keep them as a sometimes-fix rather than a food group.

foods.name: Stock cubes and stock
foods.why: Shelf-stable cubes, powders and cartons are all fine, and whatever they go into gets simmered anyway. They are salty, so they count toward a light hand with the salt shaker.

foods.name: Fairy bread
foods.why: White bread, margarine and hundreds and thousands: nothing on that plate is a safety problem. A sometimes-food by any measure, but a completely safe slice of nostalgia.

foods.name: Scones with jam and cream
foods.why: Baked scone, jarred jam and pasteurised whipped cream: every layer is green. Devonshire tea is fully on, and nobody here is weighing in on the jam-first question.

foods.name: Sticky date pudding
foods.why: Baked right through and served hot, with a butterscotch sauce that was cooked on the stove. Pub dessert menus remain very much open to you.

foods.name: Burgers, cooked through
foods.why: No pink in the patty and you are laughing, since takeaway burgers get cooked hard and fast. At fancier joints, ask whether the aioli is house-made, because that one is raw egg.

foods.name: Chicken parmigiana
foods.why: The pub legend is all clear: crumbed chicken cooked right through, ham grilled hot under the cheese, and the whole lot served bubbling. Order it with chips and no guilt.

foods.name: Eggs benedict
foods.why: The cafe classic is a double act: the poached yolk runs, and hollandaise is built on raw egg. Both are salmonella territory.
foods.makeItGreen: Ask for the eggs cooked firm and the hollandaise left off. Smashed avo, wilted spinach or a hot grilled tomato fills the gap beautifully.
foods.swap: A big brekky with firm-yolk eggs, hot bacon and avo on toast.

foods.name: Hot chips
foods.why: Deep fried and scorching hot, straight out of the fryer into the paper. About as safe as takeaway gets, and yes, the chicken salt is allowed.

foods.name: Kebab
foods.why: Meat carved hot off the spit with fresh salad is a solid feed. The wildcard is house-made garlic sauce, which is often a raw-egg job.
foods.makeItGreen: Ask for the meat hot right through, and stick to sauces poured from a commercial bottle. If the garlic sauce is made in-house, chilli or barbecue sauce has your back.

foods.name: Maccas soft serve cone
foods.why: It is the machine, not the ice cream. Soft serve dispensers are hard to clean right through, so listeria can quietly set up shop inside one.
foods.swap: A choc top, a scoop from a tub, or a frozen banana blitzed at home.

foods.name: Meat pie and sausage roll
foods.why: Baked hot and held hot, so the bakery run is a green light. The only ask is that it arrives steaming the whole way through, not warm on the outside and cool in the middle.

foods.name: Pad thai and stir-fries with sprouts
foods.why: The wok runs plenty hot, but bean sprouts usually go in at the last second and stay raw, and raw sprouts are the one listeria risk in the bowl.
foods.makeItGreen: Ask for the sprouts left out or cooked right through, then eat it fresh and steaming rather than saving half for tomorrow.

foods.name: Pho
foods.why: Depends what the beef is doing and where those sprouts end up:

variants.label: Chicken or well-done beef, sprouts wilted in the broth
variants.why: Boiling broth is your friend here. Cooked meat, plus sprouts pushed under until they soften right through, makes a lovely safe dinner.

variants.label: Rare beef slices (pho tai)
variants.why: Those pink slices only get flashed by the broth, so they count as undercooked beef.
variants.makeItGreen: Ask for the beef well done, or order the chicken one.
variants.swap: Pho ga, or a well-done brisket pho.

variants.label: Raw sprouts piled on top
variants.why: Raw bean sprouts are a known listeria carrier, even the crisp fresh-looking ones.
variants.makeItGreen: Leave them off, or drown them in the hot broth until they are cooked right through.

foods.name: Pizza
foods.why: Even the ham and the salami, because it all comes out of a screaming hot oven. Leftover slices are fine too, just send them back through the oven until they are steaming.

foods.name: Pre-packaged sandwiches and wraps
foods.why: Made hours ago, kept cold and sealed in plastic: that is exactly the set-up listeria likes, whatever the filling turns out to be.
foods.makeItGreen: Made fresh in front of you with hot fillings, or built at home that morning, and it is back on the menu.
foods.swap: A hot toastie, or a salad roll you put together yourself.

foods.name: Stuffing cooked inside the bird
foods.why: Stuffing in the cavity soaks up raw juices and often never gets hot enough in the middle, even when the bird itself is perfectly cooked.
foods.makeItGreen: Bake the stuffing in its own dish until it is piping hot, then serve it alongside. Same flavour, crispier edges, none of the risk.
foods.swap: Stuffing balls baked on their own tray.

foods.name: Sushi
foods.why: Depends how fresh it is, and what's in it:

variants.label: Made fresh in front of you, cooked fillings
variants.why: Teriyaki chicken, tinned tuna with jar mayo, avo or cucumber, rolled while you watch and eaten straight away. Sushi night is very much on.

variants.label: Raw or smoked fillings
variants.why: Sashimi, nigiri and raw salmon rolls are raw seafood, and smoked salmon rolls are chilled ready-to-eat, so both carry a listeria risk.
variants.makeItGreen: Same shop, cooked fillings: teriyaki chicken, cooked prawn, katsu or a veggie roll.
variants.swap: A cooked-roll sushi night at home, where you own the knife and the clock.

variants.label: Pre-packed or been circling a while
variants.why: Sitting time is the problem here, even with cooked fillings. Fridge sushi and long-lap train sushi have both had hours to get friendly with listeria.
variants.makeItGreen: Order it made to your order and eat it within the hour.
variants.swap: A hot chicken katsu don or a teriyaki rice bowl from the same counter.

foods.name: Sushi train
foods.why: Depends what is on the plate and how long it has been going round:

variants.label: Made fresh to order with cooked fillings
variants.why: Rolled for you and eaten straight away with cooked fillings, like teriyaki chicken, avocado or cucumber, is the green lane.

variants.label: Raw or smoked fish, or cold seafood
variants.why: Raw and cold-smoked seafood carries listeria, and so does anything cooked, chilled and left waiting.
variants.makeItGreen: Ask the kitchen for a fresh roll with cooked chicken, cooked egg or veg fillings instead.
variants.swap: A teriyaki chicken roll, made to order.

variants.label: Been circling the belt a while
variants.why: Sitting time is the risk. Even cooked fillings pick up listeria once a plate has been out of the kitchen for hours.
variants.makeItGreen: Order off the menu so it is made fresh, and eat it while it is still cold from the kitchen.

foods.name: Toasted ham and cheese
foods.why: Deli ham's redemption arc. The press takes it properly hot and heat is the one thing listeria cannot survive. Just have it steaming, not lukewarm.

foods.name: Banh mi
foods.why: The classic roll stacks pate with cold deli meats, and both are on the listeria bench. Pate doubles up with too much vitamin A, and the butter-mayo spread is often made in-house with raw egg.
foods.makeItGreen: Order the grilled chicken or grilled pork one made fresh and hot off the grill, skip the pate, and ask for sauces from a bottle rather than the house mayo.
foods.swap: A hot roast chicken roll, or a steaming banh mi style toastie at home.

foods.name: Laksa
foods.why: The coconut broth comes out close to boiling, which is exactly what you want. The catch is the handful of raw bean sprouts tossed on top at the end, because raw sprouts are a listeria risk.
foods.makeItGreen: Ask for the sprouts left out or pushed under the hot broth until they wilt right through, then eat it fresh and steaming.

foods.name: Bibimbap
foods.why: Depends what the egg on top is doing:

variants.label: Hot stone bowl, egg cooked firm
variants.why: Dolsot bibimbap arrives sizzling and keeps cooking at the table. Stir it through until the egg sets firm and everything is hot, and you are in great shape.

variants.label: Raw or runny yolk on top
variants.why: The classic raw yolk cracked over the top never really cooks, and runny egg is salmonella territory.
variants.makeItGreen: Ask for the egg fried firm, or order the hot stone version and stir until it sets right through.

foods.name: Ramen
foods.why: Depends what the egg is up to:

variants.label: Hot broth and noodles, firm egg or no egg
variants.why: The broth is kept near boiling and the cooked pork slices get a hot dunking in it. With the egg firm or skipped altogether, slurp away happily.

variants.label: Soft-centred ramen egg on top
variants.why: That marinated egg with the jammy middle is a soft-boiled egg, and runny centres are salmonella territory.
variants.makeItGreen: Ask for the egg hard boiled or left off. The broth is doing the heavy lifting in this bowl anyway.

foods.name: Dumplings and gyoza, steamed hot
foods.why: Steamed or pan fried straight from the pot and served scalding, so the filling gets cooked right through, veggie and meat ones alike. Eat them hot and fresh, not an hour later out of the container.

foods.name: Yum cha
foods.why: Depends what you lift off the trolley:

variants.label: Steamed and fried dishes, hot off the trolley
variants.why: Har gow, siu mai, pork buns and anything else that lands on the table with steam coming off it has copped the kind of heat listeria cannot survive.

variants.label: Lukewarm laps and the cold dishes
variants.why: A trolley that has been circling a while is sitting time, and sitting time is the risk. Same goes for the cold dishes, like chilled seafood and jellyfish salad.
variants.makeItGreen: Wave down the freshest trolley, take what is properly steaming, and order anything else straight from the kitchen so it arrives hot.

foods.name: Fried rice, fresh and hot
foods.why: Wok-fresh and steaming is a green light, egg and all, because everything gets cooked hard in that heat. Leftovers go in the fridge fast, get reheated once until piping hot, and are eaten within a day.

foods.name: Risotto, served hot
foods.why: Stirred over heat for ages and served hot, so everything in the pan is properly cooked. The wine is the asterisk: it simmers down to a trace, and whether a trace is fine is your care team's call, not ours.
foods.makeItGreen: Ask for it made without the wine, or make it at home with extra stock. Same comfort, no asterisk.

foods.name: Paella
foods.why: One big pan on high heat until the prawns, mussels and chicken are cooked right through. Have it fresh and steaming from the pan, and leave any mussels that stayed shut on the side.

foods.name: Butter chicken and creamy curries
foods.why: Simmered away in a hot pot until the chicken is cooked through, and the cream and yoghurt in the sauce are pasteurised. Order it fresh and properly hot with rice, and enjoy every bit.

foods.name: Rice paper rolls
foods.why: Made ahead, kept cold and eaten cold, usually wrapped around cooked prawns or chicken that has been sitting chilled for hours. That is exactly the set-up listeria likes.
foods.makeItGreen: Roll them at home with just-cooked chicken and washed veg, and eat them straight away. Same crunch, none of the sitting time.
foods.swap: Steamed dumplings, hot off the pot.

foods.name: Poke bowl with cooked fillings
foods.why: Depends what is in the bowl and who built it:

variants.label: Raw fish on top
variants.why: Raw salmon and tuna are raw seafood, so the classic poke bowl is benched for the next few months.
variants.makeItGreen: Swap the raw fish for a hot cooked topping like teriyaki chicken, straight off the grill.

variants.label: Cooked chicken or tofu from the poke bar
variants.why: Even the cooked toppings sit chilled in an open bar all day, and that is the salad-bar rule: it might not be fresh.
variants.makeItGreen: Go for the hot option if the shop has one, like a teriyaki don served steaming, or build the bowl at home.

variants.label: Built at home, eaten straight away
variants.why: Warm rice, chicken you cooked yourself, washed veg and a jar mayo drizzle. All of the fun, none of the sitting time.

foods.name: Burrito and burrito bowls
foods.why: Hot grilled meat, hot beans and melted cheese wrapped and eaten fresh is a green light, guac and sour cream included. Just check the meat and rice come out of steaming trays, not off a cold bench.

foods.name: Fish burger
foods.why: Battered or grilled, the fillet is cooked right through and served hot. The wildcard is the tartare: house-made can mean raw egg, the same asterisk the kebab wears.
foods.makeItGreen: Ask for tartare or mayo from a commercial bottle, or a squeeze of lemon instead, and it is a green light.

foods.name: Pastie
foods.why: Straight from the pie warmer and steaming through the middle, the bakery pastie follows the same happy rule as the meat pie. Just make sure the centre arrives hot, not lukewarm.

foods.name: Larb
foods.why: Classic larb can leave the mince rare or even raw, and undercooked meat is a toxoplasmosis risk. Plenty of kitchens do cook it right through, but you cannot tell by looking at the bowl.
foods.makeItGreen: Ask for the mince cooked right through and served hot, which most Thai restaurants are happy to do.
foods.swap: San choy bau, with its sizzled-hot filling.

foods.name: San choy bau
foods.why: Sizzling hot mince spooned into a crisp washed lettuce cup. The hot part is cooked right through and the cold part is just lettuce, so eat it fresh while the filling still steams.

foods.name: Tom yum soup
foods.why: It reaches the table close to boiling and the prawns cook right there in the broth. Hot, sour, safe, and surprisingly good at cutting through a queasy day.

foods.name: Thai green curry
foods.why: Simmered hot until the chicken is cooked through, with coconut milk out of a can, which is shelf-stable and safe. Order it fresh and steaming over rice and dig in.

foods.name: Katsu curry
foods.why: Crumbed chicken fried until it is golden right through, then drowned in hot curry sauce. Fully cooked and served hot is exactly the combination we like.

foods.name: Teriyaki chicken
foods.why: Grilled hot and served fresh over rice, the chicken is an easy yes. The mirin in the glaze cooks down to a trace, and trace alcohol is a care-team call, so it wears a limit instead of a free pass.
foods.makeItGreen: Ask for the glaze made without mirin, or make it at home with soy, sugar and ginger.

foods.name: Sweet and sour pork
foods.why: Battered pork fried right through and tossed in hot sauce, pineapple and all. Fully cooked, served hot, help yourself.

foods.name: Lemon chicken and honey chicken
foods.why: Battered chicken fried right through and coated in hot sauce is a green light on both counts. And yes, honey is fine for you; that famous warning is for babies under one, not mums.

foods.name: Salt and pepper tofu
foods.why: Tofu is safe the whole way through pregnancy, all soy products are, and this one gets deep fried and served hot on top of that. A double green light.

foods.name: Satay chicken skewers
foods.why: Skewers grilled hot right through, with a peanut sauce that gets simmered on the stove. Peanuts themselves are perfectly fine in pregnancy too, unless you are the one with the allergy.
